decision: Keep production Safe rendering. No Separate-mode Windows ablation or configuration change was performed.

local_release_evidence.availability: R: editor, debug export templates and release export templates
local_release_evidence.execution_scope: Help only; no scene or benchmark launched. Windows was not accessed.

current_configuration.finding: No rendering thread-model override or --render-thread option in these files. Safe follows from the pinned default; the actual Windows runtime mode was not independently queried during this review.

constraints: The CLI is parsed before project startup and can select Separate without rebuilding. It must precede the -- user-argument separator.
The pinned engine forces Safe for the editor/project manager and for builds without thread support.
The pinned documentation marks Separate experimental and unsuitable for production, with known crash risks especially around particles and window resizing; synchronization can add jitter.
The game uses particles and window-size changes. Its GPU water operations already use call_on_render_thread, but this source inspection is not a certification of Separate-mode stability.
measurement_limits: ScaleFrameBenchmark.gd:132-137 queries viewport CPU and GPU timing on every process_frame. Both getters use FUNC1RC; from a separate main thread this calls command_queue.push_and_ret and waits for completion. A Separate run would include this synchronization imposed by the benchmark.
The viewport render_cpu_ms readout excludes scripts and other engine systems, and is not total rendering CPU time: the documentation also includes frame setup and other drawn viewports in that total.

Approximately 8 ms of reported viewport rendering CPU work motivates an overlap hypothesis only. It does not establish a frame-time improvement or justify the documented production stability tradeoff.
